segments.he: עו"ש (סי' קא) כי עיקר כלל ושורש ויסוד של כל העצות להתקרב להשי"ת הוא רק אמירת תהלים ושארי תחינות ובקשות והתבודדות לפרש שיחתו בינו לבין קונו, לבקש מלפניו שיקרבו לעבודתו ית' ורק עי"ז זוכין לנצח המלחמה אם יהי' חזק ואמיץ מאד תמיד להעתיר ולהתפלל ולהתחנן לפני הש"י תמיד יהי' איך שיהי', אז בוודאי ינצח המלחמה אשרי לו, כך הבנו מדברי רבינו ז"ל כי אעפ"י שנמצאים כמה עצות טובות בספרי רבינו ז"ל שהם מלאים עצות להתקרב להשי"ת, אעפ"כ ע"פ רוב קשה להאדם לקיים העצה בעצמה, ע"כ העיקר הוא תפילות ותחינות ובקשות יהי' איך שיהי' עכ"פ ידבר בפיו באיזה בחי' שהוא ויבקש מהשי"ת תמיד שיוציא אותו מחשך לאור ויחזירהו בתשובה שלימה באמת וכו' עי"ש. הנה עין הרואה מזה ששורש ויסוד של כל העצות להתקרב להשי"ת אשר גילה רבינו הק' זצ"ל הוא עבודת התפלה, אשר ע"י עבודת התפלה זוכה האדם להתקרב להשי"ת.
segments.en: Further there [§74] copied from the Rav Yeiva: Each day a heavenly voice goes forth... "Woe to the creatures for the insult to the Torah" — meaning those who do not study for its own sake or who do not study in awe and love. Then there is insult and shame to the letters of the Torah they study — for when the letters of the Torah want to ascend upward to their root before Hashem, they are pushed downward because he did not study for its own sake or did not study in awe and love. There is no greater insult than this...

And see in Lashon Chasidim [letter Deveykus VeYichudin, §1] copied from Toldos Yaakov Yosef: The purpose of all 613 commandments is so that one may cleave to Him and love Him. And therefore they are called the 613 counsels [eitin] — for they are counsels on how to cleave to Him... And when a person cleaves and connects his thought to Him, all 248 of his limbs and 365 of his sinews are drawn after the thought... And therefore when he does one commandment with complete faith and deveykus and delight, all 613 commandments are included in it.

Further there [§5]: While he speaks in Torah and prayer, his thought should be attached to Him in deveykus and longing — in the light of the face of the living King — in the light of the Infinite within the letters. And understand — this is a great general principle in Torah and prayer, according to what I received from my teacher. And it is also propitious for nullifying judgments as I heard from him.

Further there [§11]: We find among the early ones that they performed their work through their revealed limbs while their thought and soul were cleaved to Him and to His Torah. And this is the aspect of what our Sages said: "The early ones who made their Torah primary" — meaning even when they engaged in their work their thought was fixed on their Torah and their deveykus with Hashem. And this is the aspect of "it is good to combine Torah study with a worldly occupation" — meaning not only when one is engaged in Torah and prayer should one's thought be free from worldly matters and cleave to one's Torah and prayer with Hashem — but also during that stretch of time when one engages in worldly occupation to support oneself and one's children — even so one should join Torah to it through the hidden limbs... And this is the aspect of "the hidden things belong to Hashem our G-d and the revealed things are for us and our children" — meaning even when engaged in the physical which is "for us and our children" — it should be only through the revealed — the revealed limbs — but the hidden things should even then be cleaved to Hashem our G-d.

Further there [§15 copied from Divrei Moshe]: I heard from the holy mouth of the Baal Shem Tov on the teaching of our Sages: "The conversations of Torah scholars require study." For the primary completeness of every Tzaddik is that his deveykus not be interrupted even for a single moment — even in all his speech when he must speak with people about matters necessary for worldly affairs, he should see to speak in a way that his deveykus not be interrupted, G-d forbid. And even while performing some commandment he should be very careful about this — for when he thinks about the doing of the commandment, his deveykus could be concealed from him. Therefore great alacrity is needed here.

Further there [§16]: The root of the Tzaddik's completeness is that his thought always cleave to Him — and not remove his thought from Him even for a single moment. And in all his actions — even while engaged in a physical action — he should in his thought be cleaved to Him.

And see in Derech Chasidim [letter Deveykus VeYichudin, §18] copied from Mevaser Tzedek: At the time one engages in one's worldly affairs, one must cleave to the Creator and not be separated from one's deveykus — as Rashbi said: "All my days I was bound in one bond to the Holy One blessed be He." And even at the time of Torah study it is not enough that one cleaves to the Torah in love — but one must also cleave to the hidden aspect within it, which is the Supernal Emanator, may He be blessed and exalted.

And see further there [letter Yirah Va'avodas Hashem, §78] copied from Or Torah: The primary service of the Creator is deveykus and fervor in His service and in the study of His Torah — with awe and love. And through this one can cleave to Hashem as it were.

Further there [§181] copied from Ma'or Einayim: Fear is in the aspect of "this gate belongs to Hashem" — for it is the entrance to the path of Hashem and His Torah... For whoever has fear — all wisdoms and all the Torah are within him. For in truth, whoever has no fear — grasping the Torah is impossible for him. But whoever has fear — merits and his mouth and tongue become like a flowing spring.

Further there [§187]: All the Written and Oral Torah and all the revealed commandments — these are the body of the Torah. And there is within them a life force and inwardness — the mysteries of the Torah which is His essence. And one must unify the body with the soul — that is, with the life force and inwardness that is His essence.

Further there [§195]: Fear is called a house... For as all a person's desires are kept in his home — so one who has Torah and wisdom but has no fear — they are scattered without anything to contain them. But fear contains the person so he does not go outside. And therefore fear is called a house. And this is what our Sages meant: "Whoever's fear of sin precedes his wisdom — his wisdom endures."

And see in Lashon Chasidim [letter Yirah Va'avodas Hashem, §194] copied from Ben Poras Yosef: Everything follows the intention and thought. And one can say that the deeds of the Tzaddikim when engaged in physical matters and worldly affairs are more considered before Hashem than Torah, prayer, charity, and other spiritual matters engaged in by the wicked — for everything follows the intention of the heart, as our Sages meant by "the Merciful One desires the heart." And one who engages in physical matters and his deeds are truly for the sake of Heaven, his thought and intention cleaved to Hashem — this is complete service of Hashem. And one who engages in Torah and prayer but his thought and intention are not cleaved to Hashem — he is called a rebel against Hashem. As it says: "with his mouth and lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me."

Even during study it is good to rest from one's learning from time to time and seclude one's thought in awe and reverence in deveykus with the Creator — and even if through this one is somewhat diverted from one's learning, "not the expounding is the primary thing but the deed." [Derech Chasidim, letter Torah, §18 — from Likutay Yekarim.] The intention of the study is this: when learning, for example, a teaching of Rava — one should think that Rava himself stands before him and says this thing. And then by conducting oneself thus, one draws upon oneself life force from the speech — which is the letters. And afterward when one says the law that Rava stated — one draws to oneself the life force from the understanding — for one says the law with one's intellect and comprehension. Therefore one should connect oneself and draw to oneself the life force. And one's lips will also murmur in the grave — and one also brings redemption to the world which is his body called a small world — and the redemption is the life force. [Ibid. §22, from the same.)]

Torah for its own sake — meaning: its name is Torah [Torah] — meaning it will teach and show what is concealed — which is the divine Name concealed within the Torah... And in truth to cleave to Hashem through the Torah and commandments requires many conditions as is explained in the words of our Sages. And the smallest condition of all is to be divested of the desires of the time... And in truth many among our people who appear to themselves as wise ones and great scholars in the revealed and hidden dimensions — and suppose they have come to some Torah and fear — but in truth have not yet merited even a small knowledge of the Torah of our G-d which is called Torah because it points to what is hidden within it, which is Hashem Himself. And the holy divine Reb Mendel of Premishlan said: "Hashem's Torah is perfect" — meaning Hashem's Torah specifically is perfect, that as yet no person has touched even its edge — for they learn only the externality of the Torah, with no thought to cleave to Hashem and be a chariot for Him... For they do not know at all what deveykus is or what love and fear is, and imagine that the study itself is the deveykus and the love and fear. And how can one say such a thing? For if so, they would need to be automatically clean and pure of every hint of sin and even of every hint of physical desire — for one who is truly cleaved to Hashem in love and fear in truth cannot come even to a minor sin or be attached to any desire, G-d forbid. For Hashem is holy and separated from all materiality. Rather certainly the matter of love and fear of Hashem is a different matter — it is in the heart — that the heart should be in fear of Hashem always and His love should burn in the heart always. And to this a person does not merit except through prayer with deveykus and fervor of heart, and the subjugation of all one's powers toward pure and clean thoughts for Hashem always, and separation from all pleasures, and the purity of all one's limbs and guarding them in the holiness appropriate to them, and the study of Torah for its own sake.

And the primary Torah for its own sake is to come to cleave to the One who is concealed within it... And this is what our Sages meant: "a great thing is the Divine Chariot and a small thing is the disputes of Abaye and Rava." And G-d forbid that they should call the disputes of Abaye and Rava a small thing — for this is the primary part of our holy Torah given to Moshe at Sinai. And similarly what they called the Divine Chariot a great thing — is there not today many who are expert in the writings of the holy Ari who revealed all the Divine Chariot? But in truth — whether the Torah of the revealed dimension or the Torah of the hidden dimension — everything follows the person's intentions. If his intention in it is only to know its content — he merits nothing. And about him it says "and all his kindness is like the flower of the field." But if his intention is to desire to cleave to Hashem and be a chariot for Him — and there is no path for this except through Torah and commandments — then through both the revealed and the hidden he cleaves to himself. Only that through the hidden of the Torah one merits a more wondrous deveykus. And this is what they meant: "a small thing is the disputes of Abaye and Rava" — meaning one who studies only in order to understand and know the wisdom in the Talmudic argument — this is a small thing. But one who desires to be a chariot for Hashem through Torah study — this is certainly a great thing.

I heard from the holy mouth of the holy divine Reb Dov Ber [the Maggid of Mezeritch] that one who engages in Torah for its own sake — meaning for the sake of being cleaved to Hashem, for He rests and is concentrated, as it were, in the spiritual breath of the holy Torah coming from the pure mouth of a person — then he will merit to be a chariot for Hashem. It follows that the deveykus through which he cleaves to Hashem is inward, and the words of Torah he studies are the external and garment for this deveykus — and this is correct. Contrary to this, if his desire and love are not for Hashem and he is still attached to the desires of the time and desires honor etc. — then the inward part of his thought is honor, and the Torah is the external garment of his foolish thinking. And woe to that shame — that he makes the words of Torah a garment for the inward foolishness of his thought. For deveykus with Hashem is impossible except through true humility.

I heard from Reb Menachem Mendel [of Vitebsk] that the hidden is called a thing that a person cannot explain to his friend — like the taste of food, which is impossible to relate to one who has never tasted that taste. Similarly, the love of the Creator and fear of Him — it is impossible to explain to one's friend how the love is in the heart. This is called the hidden. But what the world calls hidden — the wisdom of Kabbalah — how is it hidden? Anyone who wishes to study, the book is open before him. And if he does not understand it, he is an ignoramus, before whom the Talmud and Tosafos are also called hidden. Rather, the matter of the hidden things in the Zohar and the Ari are all built upon the matter of deveykus with the Creator — for one who merits to cleave to one's Creator and to gaze at the supernal Chariot etc.

And it is explained in Likutay Moharan Part I [Torah 12]: What we see that generally scholars oppose the Tzaddikim and speak arrogantly against the Tzaddik with pride and contempt — this is a great divine intention. For there is the aspect of Yaakov and Lavan. Yaakov is the Tzaddik who innovates true Torah innovations and studies his Torah for its own sake — and his goodness is stored and guarded and hidden for the future. And Lavan is a Torah scholar who is a wicked Jew, whose Torah is for boasting and quarreling — and such a Torah scholar — a carcass is better than him. And this is known — that one is called a Torah scholar only through the Oral Torah. For one who knows Chumash is not called a Torah scholar — only one expert in Talmud and decisors. And when he learns without knowledge he is called Lavan — after the cunning that entered him — and he hates and pursues the Tzaddik...

And when a person learns any law in holiness and purity — some law that a Tanna or other Tzaddik innovated — through this the spirit of the Tzaddik who innovated this innovation is attached to his spirit. For this law is the speech of the Tanna — and speech is life force... And when we learn the innovations of the Tzaddikim who have already gone to their world, through this their spirits are attached to ours as our Sages said: "their lips murmur in the grave." And this is the aspect of Yaakov's kiss to Rachel — and the aspect of Lavan: when the scholar knows the wisdom of Yaakov and is upright — he runs to meet him and embraces and kisses him — for through his learning the spirit of the Tanna is attached to his spirit — this is the aspect of kissing. But a wicked Jewish Torah scholar — when he learns Talmud or a legal ruling — "excessive are the kisses of an enemy" — for the Tanna cannot bear the spirit of the wicked Jewish scholar, for who can bear to kiss a carcass?

It is explained from the above that the completeness of study is when during learning one has the attachment of spirit to spirit with the spirit of the Tzaddik who innovated this innovation — and this is the drawing close to the Tzaddik. And this is the primary completeness of study. And see in Likutay Halachos [Hil. Reishis HaGez 5] where the halacha is founded on the above Torah — that all the unifications of the true Tzaddikim and their unions in the physical dimension flow only from there — the aspect of the union of Yaakov and Rachel and the kissing. But one who is not a Tzaddik and inclines toward physical desires — according to his inclination to physical desire, so he falls to the aspect of the left. And through this even all his study is in the aspect of the left... Therefore his entire rectification is only through the great true Tzaddik who is the aspect of Yaakov — who is completely holy and pure in this desire — and in both his union and his Torah study his entire intention is for Heaven alone...

And further there: "For this is known — that the entire world is maintained and governed only through the holy Torah. And if all were studying Torah purely for its own sake — without any ulterior motive whatsoever — certainly the world would already be entirely rectified — and all the divine flows and blessings would be in the world. And the primary cause of all the defects is due to disputes — for most scholars do not study for its own sake. And even those who study somewhat for its own sake — it is not yet fully clear and pure to the ultimate degree as is proper. And all their rectification is through the true Tzaddik — the aspect of Moshe — who studies Torah for its own sake to the ultimate purity — without any trace of dross whatsoever. And if all the world were to nullify themselves before him — all would be completely healed. But in our many sins — not only do they not nullify themselves before him — but they also dispute and oppose him."

And further there: "And according to the degree that one is drawn toward this desire for personal benefit — correspondingly one does not merit that one's study should be as pure and clear as is proper. And all one's rectification is only through the above great Tzaddik — who can raise everything." See there.

It is thus explained that the primary clarification and rectification and elevation of Torah — so that it be clarified to the ultimate degree of clarity — is through the true Tzaddik. And see in Likutay Halachos [Hil. Yayin Nesech 4, paragraph 28] which writes: "For the primary consolation is the holy Torah and the true Tzaddikim in every generation. For the primary consolation in all this bitter and lengthy exile is the holy Torah — as it is said 'this is my consolation in my affliction — for Your word has given me life' [Tehillim 119:50]. But not every person merits to receive good counsels from the Torah as is proper for him at every time — for he did not merit." Therefore all need the Mari Chitaya [Master of the Wheat] — which is the true Tzaddik — who clarifies and pictures for us the light of Torah for good. And this is the primary hope and consolation in all kinds of exile — in the general and the particular — physical and spiritual — in the aspect of "this one will console us from our work and from the toil of our hands" [Bereishis 5:29] — "this" is the aspect of the true Tzaddik who is called "this" — in the aspect of "for this is the whole person" [Koheles 12:13] — for the entire world was created only for "this" — and to command "this" — and "this" is equivalent. As our Sages derived from this.

When our Sages said "console, console My people" [Yeshayahu 40:1] — Nachamu nachamu — a double consolation — for we need specifically double consolations — the aspect of nachamu nachamu. That is: the consolation of the Torah — the aspect of "this is my consolation in my affliction." But from the Torah one cannot receive and draw by oneself as is proper — for one did not merit. For one can picture the light of Torah in reverse as above. Therefore we need yet another consolation upon consolation — which is the power of the true Tzaddikim — who clarify and picture for us the light of the Torah for good and for blessing — and teach us to receive true good counsels from the Torah for life and for good — and not for death and evil, G-d forbid. And this is the primary consolation. For through the portrayal of the light for good — through the true Tzaddikim — through this there are made in every place straight paths to Hashem. See there.

And see in Likutay Halachos [Hil. Oaths 2, paragraph 20] which writes: "And this is the aspect of the dispute of Korach — who separated himself from Moshe Rabbainu — who is the one through whom the Name of Hashem is primarily magnified — for through him each individual of Yisrael can have his name included in the Name of Hashem. Through being included in the name of the Tzaddik — who has already completed his name to the ultimate completion and is included in the Name of Hashem — and all who are called by the name of the Tzaddik are included in him — and through this are included in the Name of Hashem." See there.

Further there [§22]: For it is already explained that the primary wisdom is truth. And the primary thing is to understand the truth that was hidden and concealed — to merit to understand it through the strength of his faith. And for this one must toil and exert oneself greatly to seek and search for a true teacher to draw close to him. For the ultimate eternal purpose — which is the attainment of truth — is impossible except through a true teacher... For the primary master is when he can illuminate truth in the disciples — the truth of the Torah — and establish them on the truth. For even in the wisdom of the holy Torah — one who cannot establish them on the truth is not a master... And therefore the primary completeness of the master is when he can illuminate in the disciples true fear of Heaven — which is the primary purpose of the Torah... And this learning of fear of Heaven — to merit the fulfillment of the Torah — this learning is exceedingly deep and requires a very great teacher. And it is impossible to receive it except through great toil... And therefore the primary redemption depends upon drawing close to true Tzaddikim who can bring fear of Heaven and fulfillment of the Torah into the world.

And see further there [§176 from Hil. Apotekai 5]: In all of a person's service — and especially in the service of prayer — one needs great merit to be able to raise one's prayer and service to the place needed to accomplish the rectification needed in all the worlds and especially at the root of one's soul. And before the prayer and service ascend there, there are many and great dangers on the way and great responsibility from the multitude of accusers lurking on the way. Therefore the primary rectification of service — and especially the service of prayer — is through connecting everything to the true Tzaddik who is the aspect of the great lender...

Further there [§186 from Hil. HaOseh Shaliach Ligvos Chov 2]: The primary thing is to be close to the Tzaddik and cleave to him in truth at every time and moment and with every breath he breathes — drawing the spirit of life — he should immediately remember that this breath — which is his life force — is drawn from the true Tzaddik who is cleaved to the Torah and to Hashem, and he draws the spirit of holy life to everyone to complete their deficiencies. And therefore he should be careful to draw close to the Tzaddik and to Hashem with every breath — as our Sages taught: "every soul should praise G-d" — with every breath, praise G-d... It follows that the Tzaddik is in the aspect of the lender — for he lends the person the spirit of life so that afterward he can settle and repay his obligation to praise and glorify Hashem with every breath...

Further there [§201 from Hil. Sheluchin]: One must be very careful to seek and search after the true Tzaddik who has the aspect of the spirit of prophecy — holy spirit — through which the imaginative faculty is clarified and one merits complete faith... And every person in the world — from smallest to greatest — must be very careful in this all his days — to seek and search for a true teacher or a true friend who received from true Tzaddikim the words of truth that truly benefit his soul... For certainly the seeking and searching is not after the physical body of the Tzaddik — but after his holy spirit — through which the primary clarification of the imaginative faculty occurs — which is his rectification. And this one must always seek and search for...

Further there [§208]: In all the engagements one engages in — whether Torah, prayer, commandments, good deeds, or commerce and other dealings — one must intend in every action one does and every way and city and town one goes to — perhaps through this engagement and journey one will merit to find the true Tzaddik — the aspect of Moshe — upon whom all one's life and hope for eternity depends, and the life of one's children and generations to the end of all generations, and all the souls and worlds dependent upon him. And this is the aspect of: "I will rise now and go about the city, through the markets and squares — I will seek the one my soul loves."

Further there [§209]: When one merits to find the true Tzaddik — this is the aspect of morning... And therefore those true disciples engaging in Torah and prayer... and seeking and searching to find at all times more of the holy spirit of their true teacher — they are in the aspect of "watchmen for the morning, watchmen" — specifically watchmen, for they stand at their post with great strength and fortitude and they guard and wait and look forward to Hashem's salvation until they merit to find him properly...

Further there [§220]: The general principle and foundation of all the Torah is that one must be very careful not to deceive oneself in this world — for this world completely deceives a person. And just as in all business transactions one must be careful against deception and error — so too in the primary acquisition of a person in this world, which is to acquire Torah and commandments in the aspect of "truth buy" — one must also be careful against deception and error. For there are very many flaws and ulterior motives in the Torah and commandments of most of the world... And it is impossible to be fully saved from the deception and errors of this world except through drawing close to the true Tzaddik.

Further there [§221]: Every person during his study and service must connect himself to the true Tzaddikim of the generation. And then he will merit that the Tzaddik will clarify also his study and service — and through this a spiritual flow and physical flow will be drawn to all the dwellers above and below.

Further there [§231]: One who does not merit to know of the true Tzaddik — the aspect of the point of truth — the aspect of Yaakov — even if he is an upright G-d-fearing person who prays and engages in Torah — most of the time all his service is in bitterness without any life force and fervor and warmth of holiness. And Hashem has no delight from such service for it is in the aspect of sleep. But the true Tzaddik — the aspect of Yaakov — draws true Torah innovations in such wondrous and awesome ways and such wondrous and awesome intellects — until he places and inserts the true intellect into the very marrow of the minds of those who draw close to him — planted deeply — so that no error of the imaginative faculty will have power to remove them from this, G-d forbid. For they already understand the truth to its truthfulness very clearly and very thoroughly. And through this they merit to serve Hashem with wholeness and great holy fervor...

Further there [§235]: The primary completeness of the Tzaddik's attainment is when he merits through his attainment of the hidden aspects of the Torah — to draw through this counsels and ways and paths and stratagems for how to bring Yisrael to deed and to the fulfillment of the Torah. For "not the expounding is the primary thing but the deed."

Further there [§251]: The primary rectification of Torah study is through the aspect of the Tzaddik. And whoever separates the aspect of the scholar from the aspect of the Tzaddik — and says that Torah study itself is the primary thing and pays no attention to rectifying his deeds — and is certainly not subservient to the true Tzaddik, and all the more so when he disputes against him, G-d forbid — he has not merited, and it becomes for him a poison of death. For he forms the letters of the Torah in the opposite direction, G-d forbid... But even one who does not merit to be himself in the aspect of a Tzaddik completely — even so, if he at least subjugates himself under the Tzaddik like a slave under his master — then all his Torah and study and all his deeds receive rectification through the true Tzaddik who forms everything for good. And then it is said of him as well: "he merited — it becomes for him a potion of life" — through the power of the true Tzaddik.

It is explained from all the above that the primary completeness of service is specifically through drawing close to true Tzaddikim. And it is explained in the holy books that what our Sages taught: "I created the evil inclination, I created the Torah as its spice" — this specifically refers to Torah that one studies for its own sake. And to merit Torah for its own sake is through drawing close and attachment to Tzaddikim. And see in Atzas Shalom [letter Talmud Torah, §98]: One who connects himself during his study to the true Tzaddik and the upright ones of the generation — through this the study ascends to the Shechinah through the Tzaddik... It is explained from this that through attachment to the Tzaddik, the study ascends to the Shechinah.

And see further there [§102]: The primary flaw of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil was that it did not include together the aspects of scholar and Tzaddik — which is the flaw of scholars who dispute against the Tzaddikim. They say the primary thing is only the study itself and one does not need to draw close to Tzaddikim or to rectify one's deeds at all. And ultimately neither of these came to fruition for them — for afterward they cast even Torah study behind their backs, as is unfortunately found with many people who in their youth engaged in Torah somewhat and afterward completely threw off the yoke of Torah... and all of this because they paid no attention to rectifying their deeds and did not strive to draw close to true Tzaddikim... For in truth the primary rectification of Torah study is through the aspect of the Tzaddik. And one who separates the aspect of the scholar from the aspect of the Tzaddik is in the aspect of one who cut down the plantings... When the scholar is subservient to the Tzaddik — then he merits to form the letters of the Torah for good through the power of the Tzaddik who is the true teacher. But when he is not subservient to him and all the more so when he disputes against him, G-d forbid — he has not merited and it becomes a poison of death for him — for he forms the letters of the Torah in the opposite direction through his separating the aspect of the scholar from the aspect of the Tzaddik.

And we find in several books that addressed the study of mussar [ethical guidance] and found inadequacy in Torah study alone. And see Sefer HisRageshus HaLev [§1] which brings there from Sefer Maskil el Dal which wrote on the teaching of our Sages [Brachos 5a]: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: always let a person provoke his good inclination against his evil inclination... Rashi explains: if he overcomes it, well and good — and if not, let him engage in Torah. He should have said "let him study Torah" — and it seems to me that precisely "in your heart" is specified — because what our Sages taught: "I created the evil inclination, I created the Torah as its spice" and "if this contemptible one meets you, drag him to the study house — if he is stone he will melt, if he is iron he will shatter" — this is not a clear-cut matter that the Torah is a remedy and spice against the evil inclination. For our Sages taught: "he merited — it becomes a potion of life, he did not merit — it becomes a poison of death" — meaning when one does not study in order to do. And it is written "I wisdom dwell with cunning" — once a person studies Torah, cunning enters him. And it is taught in the Baraisa of Avos: "one who studies Torah for its own sake draws him close to merit and distances him from sin." It is made explicit that only Torah study for its own sake has this virtue — to be a spice against the evil inclination. And one who studies Torah not for its own sake — for whatever ulterior motive — only his mouth studies Torah but not his heart. And in contrast, one who studies for its own sake and says each day with tears of love "I give thanks before You that You placed my portion among those who sit in the study house" — for him mouth and heart are equal... And this is what Dovid said: "be provoked" as above — and if he has not overcome it let him engage in Torah — meaning the Torah that is a spice — and which Torah is a spice? Torah that one studies for its own sake.

And see further there which brings from Sefer Ma'amar Yedi'ah B'Techilah: "If you search for it like silver" [Mishlei 2:4] etc. — and I add to it: it does not say "then you will fear Hashem" but "then you will understand" — meaning that you will understand what fear of Hashem is and you will understand the ways of the evil inclination and its stratagems. But you are still not safe from stumbling — and sometimes you will win and sometimes you will lose. And if one does not search like silver — one will not understand at all what fear of Hashem is and will consider oneself a Tzaddik in all one's ways and will sometimes win and a thousand times lose. But to merit the level of the true Tzaddik — so as never to lose — this is exceedingly difficult and requires heavenly assistance to separate the kelipah from holiness completely. And even if you study all the holy books it will not help — except for thoughts of repentance at the time of the act, as is known to every truly wise person... For from the language "then you will understand" it appears that even after the toil one arrives only at understanding... if one does not study mussar — one wins sometimes and loses a thousand times and does not understand what fear of Hashem is and considers oneself a Tzaddik. And through mussar one recognizes one's own smallness and only sometimes loses and sometimes wins. And if through understanding fear of Hashem one merits to reach the excellent level in fear of Hashem — one can reach holy spirit. And about this the Jerusalem Talmud says [Shabbos 1]: "fear of sin leads to holy spirit" and it says "then you will understand the fear of Hashem and knowledge of G-d you will find" — meaning if one merits to complete oneself in the attribute of fear — for everything is included in "then you will understand" — that through understanding one can merit to ascend from level to level in fear of Hashem up to the level that brings holy spirit. And understanding of fear of Hashem is the opening to enter into the level of fear.

And see further there in the same book [§2, §4] which brings from Likutay Mussar of the Maharya Azulai: Those Torah scholars who do not wish to study mussar — for the most part they become arrogant in their learning and think they are great wise men. And they are not careful to pray properly and cause flaws in the covenant of the tongue and circumcision and the like. And therefore their Torah is not acceptable — for it is not for its own sake. But Torah scholars whom the fear of Hashem has touched in their hearts will hasten to repent and study mussar and immediately recognize their arrogance and the nature of their study and what they stumble in — and they will repent before Hashem. And then their study will ascend to the will of Hashem. And it brings there further from Peleh Yo'etz [letter Mussar]: it is known and famous — the virtue of mussar study — until the commentators explained that what our Sages said "I created the evil inclination, I created the Torah as its spice" is all about the study of mussar. And we brought above that this refers to the study of the hidden — and one can say that the study of the hidden is in truth the study of mussar.

It further brings there from Reishis Chochmah [Gate of Teshuvah, end of ch. 2]: Before regret and repentance, one's Torah is not acceptable... And for this the pious Rabbi Yose ben Elai had intention when he said "happy is one whose toil is in Torah and who gives satisfaction to his Maker" — meaning one who engages in it clean from sin and transgression, for then the King delights in him and in his Torah. And this was the virtue of the early ones — that their Torah was so acceptable that they were even exempt from prayer — for their Torah was clean... For through Torah study a person draws the Shechinah upon himself, and when he is clean of sin the Shechinah found a throne and resting place in which to sit and rest — like a person sitting in a properly arranged chair where the chair gives him pleasure. So too the Torah needs to be a properly arranged throne to draw the Shechinah to sit in it. But when a person is stained with the stains of sins — the Torah does not rest in him, for there is no throne for either Torah or the Shechinah to reside in... Therefore first one must do teshuvah properly and then engage in Torah... And the primary Torah is the teshuvah and the deed.

Further there from Ya'aros Devash [Part 1, Homily 1]: Now we have already said that these days are fitting to fix in Torah — for it is a potion of life. But in truth for penitents as we are — the majority of us in our many sins require prayer. For without prayer and supplication our Torah does not help — for in a place of filth the Torah is repugnant. And we are full of filth in our many sins and pollutions. But through prayer Hashem will wash the daughters of Tzion... One who sees understands that even the mighty ones of Torah in previous generations — such as the holy and awesome Gaon Reb Yehonasan of blessed memory, who was a pillar of Torah — wrote such words: "our Torah does not help" and "we are full of filth" — and wrote that through prayer Hashem will wash away the filth... And see in the introduction to Sefer HishtapchusHaNefesh which speaks there of the virtue of prayer and hisbodidus — and that this holy path is the ancient path on which our fathers and prophets and holy teachers always walked. And all the disciples of the holy Baal Shem Tov walked in this path. Until our holy master Rabbainu came — who engaged greatly in prayer and supplications and hisbodidus in fields and forests — and said that all his engagement was prayer. And he revealed to us that there is no counsel to be saved from the great intensification of the evil inclination that always hungers and desires to make a person stumble — except through hisbodidus: that each person, according to what he knows of the wounds of his heart and the pains of his soul, should set for himself a special place to pour out his heart before Hashem — whatever passes over him, in the language in which we speak — and to ask Him to draw him close to His service. And he said that prayer is the general counsel and root of all the counsels brought in his holy books. And he said that from smallest to greatest, a Yisraeli cannot exist except through hisbodidus. And he said that the primary weapon of the Yisraeli to overcome his evil inclination is only prayer and hisbodidus. And see in Sichos HaRan at its beginning in the accounts of his conduct and his toil in divine service — that the primary service through which he merited what he merited was only through the abundance of prayers and supplications and requests and appeasements — and he was accustomed greatly to pray and beseech before Him and to appease and entreat Him with all kinds of supplications and requests that He grant him merit to draw close to His service. And the primary thing that helped him was prayer in the Yiddish language spoken among us... And this is the primary thing that helped him to merit what he merited.

Further there [§154]: He said: the primary thing through which he reached his level was only through the matter of simplicity [Prastik] — that he spoke greatly and conversed much between himself and his Maker — and said much Tehillim in simplicity. And through this specifically he reached what he reached. And see in the conversations written at the end of Likutay Moharan [there §96]: He said that speech has very great power — for one can whisper over a rifle barrel so that it cannot shoot. And understand this.

And there [§98]: He said further regarding strengthening oneself in hisbodidus and supplications and requests — that speech has great power to arouse a person even though it seems to the person that he has no heart. Even so, when he speaks many words of arousal and supplications and requests and the like — this itself that he speaks is the aspect of the revelation of his heart's and soul's arousal to Hashem. In the aspect of: "my soul went out at his speaking" [Shir HaShirim 5:6] — that the speaking itself is the revelation of the soul and heart. And sometimes through speaking much — even if he is completely without any heart — even so he will come through this afterward to great heart-arousal. And the general principle: speech itself has great power.

Further there [§100]: They related to me that he said: from smallest to greatest it is impossible to be a truly upright person except through hisbodidus. And he mentioned many many famous true Tzaddikim and said that all of them came to their level only through hisbodidus.

Further there [§101]: For the general principle, root, and foundation of all the counsels to draw close to Hashem is only the saying of Tehillim and other supplications and requests — and hisbodidus to pour out one's speech between oneself and one's Maker — to ask before Him to draw one close to His service. And only through this does one merit to overcome the battle — if one is strong and mighty always to entreat and pray and beseech before Hashem always, whatever the situation. Then certainly one will overcome the battle. Thus we understood from Rabbainu's words — for even though there are many good counsels in Rabbainu's books that are full of counsels to draw close to Hashem — even so, for the most part it is hard for a person to fulfill the counsel itself. Therefore the primary thing is prayers and supplications and requests — whatever the situation — at least let him speak with his mouth in whatever aspect he is able, and ask Hashem always to take him out of darkness to light and return him in complete teshuvah in truth. One who sees from this: that the root and foundation of all the counsels to draw close to Hashem that our holy master revealed is the service of prayer — through which a person merits to draw close to Hashem.
